messages:
maya: heads-up — canary runs after today's merge (PR #4123) show decode p95 ~2x for long-context chat workloads. noticed right after the rollout. :eyes:

omar: same here, popped in dashboards at 11:13 UTC. tail latency +110ms on 2k token traces. not universal but high-ctx heavy.

liam: what changed in the merge? any kernel swaps or batching tweaks?

maya: primary change is the new kernel selector heuristic (prefer fused-attn when seq_len > 512) + small rework in batching to prefer fewer microbatches for better throughput. also touched KV eviction policy (slightly lower threshold).

ingrid: perf-bot CI summary just posted: 
perf-bot: CI perf diff for commit 0f3a..d9e7 — decode_p95 +85%, decode_p50 +10%, tail token throughput -18% on large-context perf suite. See: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/6123

omar: looks like fused-attn path is being chosen but falling back mid-decode to generic kernel, causing double work? profiler shows hop between attn_fused->attn_generic in same request.

liam: can you paste the short flame snippet?

maya: quick prof snippet from a repro run (reduced):
```
flame: decode loop
  40% attn_fused_forward
  35% attn_generic_forward
  15% kv_cache_serialize
  10% other
```

maya: threads show attn_fused invoked, then attn_generic for subsequent layers. seems like kernel chooser flipping at layer boundary.

ingrid: that could explain bad cache/locality thrash — switching kernels invalidates compiled buffers and forces reconfig. also the KV eviction tweak may be increasing cache churn for long seqs.

omar: I repro locally with unit test harness. added a verbose trace: 
```
[TRACE] kernel_selector: selected fused-attn (seq=1024, batch=1, qkv_layout=packed)
[TRACE] compile_cache: miss for fused-attn; triggering compile
[TRACE] kernel_selector: falling back to attn-generic at layer 4 (shape mismatch)
```

omar: "shape mismatch" is suspicious — we didn't change layout code in this PR. could be an interaction with the batching rework that sometimes splits microbatches unevenly.

liam: can we bisect the merge set? what's the minimal suspect range (author, commit list)?

maya: suspect commits: 0f3a (batching heuristics rewrite), 4b2d (kernel selector heuristic), 9c11 (kv eviction tweak). start with 4b2d/0f3a.

ingrid: plan: 1) hold canary rollout (set rollout=0.0) 2) run perf bisect across 0f3a..d9e7 focusing on decode_p95/flake suite 3) try reverting 4b2d (kernel selector heuristic) as a hot revert if bisect pins it.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused for release/2026-03-09-merge by ingrid.

maya: I started a bisect job on infra (perf-bisect.sh) against the repro harness, will report back with the first bad commit candidate.

perf-bot: queued perf-bisect job #789 — estimated completion ~45m. will post per-commit diffs.

omar: meanwhile, small experiment: force kernel_selector to prefer attn_generic for all layers — p95 drops back to baseline in canary. indicates selector is root cause, not fused kernel itself.

liam: good quick test. if selector logic is nondeterministically flipping due to batch split/shape rounding, we should make it deterministic (tie-break on compiled-kernel-availability) until we resolve.

ingrid: agree. can we add a short-term fix: selector prefers already-compiled kernel for same request if that avoids fallback mid-run? low-risk change and can be hotfixed.

maya: I'll draft a tiny guard: if compiled_cache.has(selected_kernel) or previous_layer_kernel == selected_kernel then prefer it. push as hotfix PR 4127.

omar: also add assert in tests for consistent kernel per-request for given shapes.

sre-oncall: from SRE side, holding canary is correct. if you push hotfix we can do a limited canary with single cluster and watch telemetry.

maya: PR 4127 opened. small compile guard + extra unit test. request review from liam and ingrid.

liam: reviewing now. quick question about fallback safety: ensure we don't force a bad kernel when it's actually incompatible — need safe check on shape/compiler flags.

maya: yes added an explicit compatibility check before preferring.

perf-bot: perf-bisect update: first pass narrowed to range 4b2d..9c11; earliest commit showing significant delta is 4b2d (kernel selector heuristic). full bisect finishing ~20m.

marek: (ops) FYI this hit two downstream customers in staging, flagged by CS. they're paused on canary usage.

ingrid: if bisect confirms 4b2d, we ship revert 4b2d+hotfix 4127 together and re-run canary.

maya: bisect finished — culprit commit = 4b2d (kernel selector heuristic). decode_p95 +92% on repro. attaching commit note: "prefer fused-attn when seq>512".

omar: ok revert prepared (PR 4130). reverting heuristic and land hotfix 4127 in same deploy.

deploy-bot: Revert PR 4130 and Hotfix PR 4127 queued for canary deployment.

ingrid: after revert+hotfix we should keep the change behind a feature flag and add more e2e coverage with mixed microbatch splits and long ctx.

liam: also let's add telemetry in kernel_selector that increments a per-request "kernel_switch_count" metric so we can detect flip thrash early. low overhead.

maya: agreed. I'll follow up with a tiny metric patch.

sre-oncall: monitoring note — if canary shows regression again, escalate to oncall immediately.

maya: thanks all. summary: 4b2d caused flaky kernel selection leading to mid-run fallbacks; bisect confirmed; revert + hotfix queued; we'll add determinism and metrics.

omar: :thumbsup: nice bisecting teamwork.

perf-bot: CI post-revert: decode_p95 back to baseline (within noise). closing perf-bisect job #789.

maya: closing thread once deploy stabilizes, will ping post-canary status.

ingrid: please drop the replay commands used for repro in the follow-up note so infra can run it nightly.

maya: will do.
